title: August and the Extraction
premise: Yara Nakamura, a financial-crimes investigator at a compliance firm, notices a charter flight's records erased mid-flight — the plane, its passengers, and a shell-company payment trail all blinking out of existence. Following the vanished money, Yara uncovers a plot to stage a catastrophic industrial 'accident' at a coastal refinery, laundered through the same clean-money networks Yara spends their days legitimizing. Hunted by the private security firm executing the plan and betrayed by their own employer, Yara teams with a disgraced air-traffic controller who was meant to be a patsy. Together they expose the attack publicly at the cost of Yara's career, identity, and safety — ending with Yara walking away with a new name, the evidence released, and justice served entirely outside the law.
about_author: Lior Joubert is the pen name of a former regulatory analyst who spent a decade tracing money across borders before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside systems designed to look clean.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. We meet Yara mid-audit, laundering legitimacy for a bank, go-bag packed in the closet, lie about their past polished and rehearsed. A routine flag on a charter payment nags at them. Emotional beat: competent loneliness, the sense that survival has become a habit rather than a life.

chapters.title: Flight 4417
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. While reconciling overnight transactions, every record of charter flight 4417 evaporates — manifests, payment, even the airframe's registration. Yara screenshots what they can before the system wipes itself. Emotional beat: the cold thrill of a real anomaly breaking through a numb routine.

chapters.title: Clean Money, Dirty Hands
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara traces the payment to a shell network their own firm validated months ago. Their supervisor, Dana, warns them off with unusual force. Emotional beat: the first crack of dread — the machine Yara serves may be the crime.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't on the Plane
chapters.summary: Controller POV (Ezra Voss). Ezra, a suspended air-traffic controller, receives a settlement offer tied to an NDA about a flight he never worked — 4417. He realizes he's being positioned as a scapegoat. Emotional beat: paranoid humiliation curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Yara finds Ezra through the NDA's law firm and they meet in a transit station, trading fragments: a vanished flight, a framed controller, a payment routed through Meridian Coastal Energy. Emotional beat: two strangers deciding to trust each other out of necessity.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Under a pretext audit, Yara visits the Meridian refinery and sees security contractor Halcyon Risk Group running an unscheduled 'safety drill' — the same firm paid via the shell network. Emotional beat: dread made physical; the accident has a rehearsal.

chapters.title: What the Drill Was For
chapters.summary: Ezra's POV. Ezra pulls archived radar data showing 4417's flight path over the refinery's fuel depot before its records vanished. The 'drill' mapped evacuation gaps. Emotional beat: the plot snaps into focus and feels enormous.

chapters.title: Dana
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara confronts Dana, who admits the firm validated Meridian's structures under pressure and begs Yara to drop it — then quietly deletes Yara's access. Emotional beat: betrayal by the last institution Yara half-trusted.

chapters.title: Halcyon Days
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV (Kessler, Halcyon operations lead). Kessler flags an internal anomaly — Yara's audit trail — and orders surveillance, preferring a quiet disappearance over noise. Emotional beat: bureaucratic menace; murder as logistics.

chapters.title: The Tail
chapters.summary: Yara and Ezra POV. Yara spots surveillance outside their apartment and triggers the go-bag plan they've rehearsed for years. The polished lie about their past becomes their escape route. Emotional beat: survival instinct finally has a purpose.

chapters.title: Off the Grid
chapters.summary: Yara and Ezra POV. Hiding in a marina safehouse, they decode the shell network and find a countdown: the 'accident' is scheduled in nine days, timed to a futures position that shorts Meridian's insurer. Emotional beat: grim clarity — profit is the motive, timing is the weapon.

chapters.title: The Buyer
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara meets a broker from the network who, believing Yara is a rival launderer, reveals Halcyon's client: a holding company owned by Meridian's own chairman, cashing out before the refinery burns. Emotional beat: vertigo — the victim is the arsonist.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Yara and Ezra build a case: flight data, payment trail, the drill schedule. Every official channel is compromised — regulators, police, press contacts all touch Halcyon. Emotional beat: the closing of lawful doors; justice must be extralegal.

chapters.title: Kessler Closes
chapters.summary: Kessler POV and Yara POV. Halcyon raids the marina; Ezra is taken, Yara escapes with a copied drive but a bullet graze. Emotional beat: terror and guilt — Yara's investigation cost someone else.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Ezra's POV. Kessler offers Ezra freedom for the drive's location, revealing the attack will be blamed on Ezra's 'sabotage' of refinery systems. Ezra stalls, buying time, planting doubt. Emotional beat: a coward learning to be brave under pressure.

chapters.title: The Chairman's Ledger
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Following the holding company, Yara reaches the chairman's estranged daughter, who provides the ledger linking him to the shorts and Halcyon's contract — motive, means, and signature. Emotional beat: unexpected alliance; even gilded families bleed.

chapters.title: Six Days
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara negotiates with a journalist and a federal auditor in parallel, knowing either could sell them out. They set a deadman's-switch release. Emotional beat: the exhausting arithmetic of trust with a clock running.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara infiltrates the Halcyon facility where Ezra is held, using the refinery drill schedules as cover. They extract Ezra in a chaotic escape that Halcyon must conceal rather than report. Emotional beat: adrenaline and the strange intimacy of risking everything for a near-stranger.

chapters.title: The Trigger
chapters.summary: Kessler POV. With the plan compromised, Kessler's client orders the attack moved up — 48 hours — and Kessler begins erasing his own team. Emotional beat: the machine devouring its hands.

chapters.title: Refinery
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. Yara and Ezra infiltrate the refinery during a forced shutdown drill, physically preventing the staged ignition while the deadman's switch dumps the ledger, flight data, and Halcyon contract to press and regulators worldwide. Kessler is killed by his own employers mid-operation. Emotional beat: desperate, kinetic, costly.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The chairman is arrested; the firm implodes; Dana testifies. Yara, officially a fugitive who 'died' in the marina raid, watches the reckoning from the edges. Emotional beat: hollow triumph — justice done, life as known it gone.

chapters.title: August
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, coda. Under a new name in a new city, Yara unpacks the go-bag for the first time in years — then packs it again, out of habit, then leaves it open, empty. Emotional beat: cautious peace; survival finally distinct from living.
